stem_book: Which of the following correctly explains why ionization energy, separation energy and excitation energy are always positive? (a) Electron already has positive total energy in all states (b) Energy must always be supplied to increase the energy of a bound electron (c) Electron releases energy when it moves to higher energy levels (d) Total energy is always positive in all stationary orbits
key: b Energy must always be supplied to increase the energy of a bound electron
derived: b Energy must always be supplied to increase the energy of a bound electron
correct_answer: b Energy must always be supplied to increase the energy of a bound electron
work: E_n < 0 and rises toward 0 with n; any upward move (excite/separate/ionise) needs ΔE = E_final − E_initial > 0 supplied
